topic.focus: insider trading filings (Form 4) as a predictive equity signal
topic.angle: cluster buys, officer vs director buys, net insider buying rate

papers.title: Synthesizing Information-Driven Insider Trade Signals
papers.hypothesis: Rank stocks by a composite of multiple insider-trade signals (recency, trade size, officer-vs-director role, cluster count) normalized into a single cross-sectional score; long the top decile.
papers.rationale: Heckmann, Jacobs & Schwarz (2023, SSRN 4537187) test a composite that synthesizes several academic insider-trade signals across an international panel; long-short generates significant alpha in ~2/3 of countries, predominantly in equal-weighted portfolios. The composite approach is robust to individual-signal noise, making it directly translatable as a ranking layer in a cross-sectional strategy. The 2-day skip accounts for Form 4 filing lag post-SOX.

papers.title: Do Insiders Cluster Trades with Colleagues? Evidence from Daily Insider Trading
papers.hypothesis: Score each stock by the count of distinct insiders who filed open-market purchases within a 42-day rolling window; stocks with ≥3 clustered buyers rank highest and are held for 21 days.
papers.rationale: Alldredge & Blank (Journal of Financial Research, 2019) find cluster purchases generate 2.1% abnormal return over 21 days vs 1.2% for solitary buys; 90-day abnormal return gap widens to 2.5%. The signal is consistent with information sharing among insiders rather than coincidence. Implementable as a simple count of distinct Form 4 filers within 42 trading days, filtered to direct open-market purchases only.

papers.title: Decoding Inside Information
papers.hypothesis: Classify each insider as 'opportunistic' (no predictable calendar pattern in prior 3 years) and use only their buy filings as a cross-sectional ranking signal; ignore 'routine' traders.
papers.rationale: Cohen, Malloy & Pomorski (NBER/RFS) show opportunistic buys predict next-quarter returns with 4-factor alpha of ~82 bps/month; routine buys show near-zero alpha. Requiring 3 years of history to classify each filer eliminates most noise and mechanically filters out grants/awards. This filter is straightforward to layer on top of any Form 4 pipeline and is the single highest-confidence separator in the literature.

papers.title: Herding Insider Traders: The Case of Opportunistic Insiders
papers.hypothesis: Measure the net insider buying rate among opportunistic officers (CFO, CEO, COO) only within a 63-day window, weighting by trade-size USD; rank stocks by this officer-specific net buy rate for a 21-day hold.
papers.rationale: MDPI 2025 paper on herding among opportunistic insiders finds that clustering behavior amplifies return predictability specifically for C-suite officers who are classified as opportunistic traders. Combining the officer-role filter with the opportunistic classification and a net-buy-rate metric (buys minus sells / total insider volume) yields a stronger signal than either filter alone, particularly for mid- and large-cap stocks in the Russell 1000 universe.

papers.title: Insider Filings as Trading Signals — Does It Pay to Be Fast?
papers.hypothesis: Reacting intraday to Form 4 filings to capture short-horizon abnormal returns is not scalable; dollar-adjusted returns are negative after realistic position sizing and transaction costs.
papers.rationale: Oenschläger & Möllenhoff (Finance Research Letters, Nov 2024) find positive percentage abnormal returns for very short holds (1-5 days) but negative USD-adjusted returns once realistic position sizing is applied; returns are negatively correlated with liquidity. This is an important negative result: the signal should be used at longer holding horizons (21-63 days) and with a universe liquidity filter, not exploited intraday. Supports using insider signals in a weekly or monthly rebalanced cross-sectional strategy.
